The pinned text-only V4.1 renderer rejects image content instead of producing a prompt. The dependency/source mismatch is confirmed; no fresh deployed-GPU reproduction is claimed in this issue.

## Environment

- Dynamo base: `843d92a7e4170ef6daf8a27aac906af6917bc376` (1.6.0 development line).
- Baseline dependencies: `dynamo-renderer 5.3.1`, `dynamo-protocols 6.0.1`.
- Patch validation: macOS ARM64, Rust 1.96.1; CPU-only renderer integration tests.
- The deployment operator confirms that the container build has been tested in production. The image digest and exact source-commit mapping are not recorded here.

## Additional Context

Implementation: #15165, commit `ff54cabba7f1675b3972a226cea7a321751d93cc`.

- Consumes https://github.com/ai-dynamo/frontend-crates/pull/254 via renderer 5.3.2 and its required protocols 6.1.0 dependency.
- All three focused integration tests pass; the PR's Rust tests, Clippy, pre-commit, DCO, and aggregate pre-merge checks pass.
- Out-of-order tool-result media alignment is a separate issue addressed by #15097 / #15152. The implementation PR is ready for review; those companion fixes remain relevant for conversations with out-of-order image-bearing tool results.

title: webhook validation test pins encoding/json's incidental struct name, fails under Go 1.27
body:
## Describe the Bug

`internal/webhook/validation` has one table test whose expected error string
embeds an `encoding/json` implementation detail — the outermost Go struct
type name that `json.UnmarshalTypeError` prints ahead of the field path
(e.g. `Go struct field PodCliqueSet.spec.template.topologyConstraint.pack`).
That name is not a function of `deploy/operator/internal/provideroverride`'s
code; it comes straight from `encoding/json`, and Go 1.27 changed which
unqualified type name lands there for a pointer-typed nested field. The
webhook's own behavior (reject the malformed value, don't echo it) is
unchanged either way.

`deploy/operator/go.mod` declares `go 1.26.6` — a minimum, not a pin — so any
`make test` / `make envtest` run outside the operator's Docker image (which
does pin `golang:1.26.6` in `deploy/operator/Dockerfile`) already reproduces
this under a Go 1.27 toolchain, even on an unrelated change.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install a Go 1.27.x toolchain (verified with 1.27.0).
2. `cd deploy/operator && make envtest` (or `go test
   ./internal/webhook/validation/...` with `KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS` set).

## Expected Behavior

`TestDynamoGraphDeploymentValidator_Validate` passes, matching CI (which
pins Go 1.26.5/1.26.6 via `actions/setup-go` and the Docker base image).

## Actual Behavior

```
--- FAIL: TestDynamoGraphDeploymentValidator_Validate/malformed_provider_override_field_is_invalid_without_echoing_its_value
    admission errors = [... Go struct field PodCliqueSet.spec.template.topologyConstraint.pack ...],
    want [... Go struct field TopologyConstraint.spec.template.topologyConstraint.pack ...]
```

Verified against the exact pinned `github.com/ai-dynamo/grove/operator/api`
version in `go.sum`: `go1.26.6` produces `TopologyConstraint.`, `go1.27.0`
produces `PodCliqueSet.` for the identical input and dependency graph.

## Environment

Linux amd64, Go 1.26.6 vs Go 1.27.0 (both from go.dev/dl), operator module
at `go.mod`'s pinned `github.com/ai-dynamo/grove/operator/api
v0.1.0-alpha.12-rc1`.

title: [BUG]: Multimodal loaders ignore the configured media file size limit
body:
### Describe the Bug

The shared multimodal image, audio, and video loaders call the HTTP fetcher without a byte limit. Dynamo already defines DYN_MM_MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB with a 64 MiB default in the media-reference path, but that limit is not applied to the main loader paths.

As a result, a large remote media response is fully buffered before decoding, and batches can download several items concurrently. This can cause unexpectedly high memory usage or terminate a frontend/worker under memory pressure.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a multimodal vLLM frontend/worker using the documented Python chat processor path.
2. Submit a chat request containing an image_url, audio_url, or video_url whose server returns a response larger than the configured media limit.
3. Observe that the loader continues buffering the response instead of raising UrlValidationError at the configured limit.

A source-level reproduction is also visible by inspecting the fetch_bytes calls in image_loader.py, audio_loader.py, and video_loader.py: they pass policy but not max_bytes. The local_media_reference path does pass max_bytes.

### Expected Behavior

All remote multimodal loader paths should honor DYN_MM_MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB (64 MiB by default), reject oversized responses while streaming, and return the existing client-facing validation error.

### Actual Behavior

The image, audio, and video loaders leave max_bytes unset, so collect_capped buffers the complete response. DYN_MM_MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB only protects local_media_reference.

### Environment

- Branch: main
- Commit: 78310370b5ea
- Components: dynamo.common.multimodal image/audio/video loaders and dynamo.common.http
- Reproduced by executing the repository collect_capped implementation and inspecting the loader call arguments.

### Additional Context

The three batch loaders use asyncio.gather, so multiple media items in one request can amplify peak memory usage. A focused fix can reuse max_media_bytes() for all three HTTP(S) calls and add regression tests that assert the resolved cap is forwarded.

title: [BUG]: vllm-omni-video-agg on 1.4.2 drops base64 delivery and corrupts video colors
body:
## Describe the bug

Case-level follow-up to #13383 and its [earlier validation report](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/13383#issuecomment-5594559029). This issue tracks **`vllm-omni-video-agg`** specifically so the corresponding local workflow and Kubernetes translation can have explicit pass/fail acceptance criteria.

On matched public Dynamo **1.4.2** images, startup/model discovery succeed, but generation has two independently observed defects:

1. `response_format=b64_json` is dropped; the completed response contains only a pod-local `file://` URL.
2. The recovered video has severe color corruption from the bundled FFmpeg path.

These are not worker-startup failures and are not cured by aligning the operator to the same release.

## Local script and source DGD being mirrored

- **Originating local launcher:** [`examples/backends/vllm/launch/agg_omni_video.sh`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/0873e6c52d13ebb571b7205b1eda7d523b2d5335/examples/backends/vllm/launch/agg_omni_video.sh) (immutable upstream snapshot; byte-identical to the local script used as the template).
- **Candidate Kubernetes counterpart:** [`examples/backends/vllm/deploy/agg_omni_video.yaml`](https://github.com/Jont828/dynamo/blob/72914d15522833cda4c449094c49698c95497ab9/examples/backends/vllm/deploy/agg_omni_video.yaml) at example-branch commit `72914d15522833cda4c449094c49698c95497ab9`.
- The DGD counterpart is currently on the example branch, **not** a claim that this manifest ships in the 1.4.2 release or exists on upstream `main`.

The mapping preserves one frontend, one GPU worker, the model, output modality, media path, and relevant backend flags. The source script supplies local port/memory-budget helpers; Kubernetes supplies discovery/system-port wiring, placement, and an existing model-cache mount.

Core worker command represented in the DGD:

```bash
python3 -m dynamo.vllm.omni \
  --model Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers \
  --output-modalities video \
  --media-output-fs-url file:///tmp/dynamo_media \
  --enforce-eager
```

The frontend is the operator-managed equivalent of `python -m dynamo.frontend`.

## Deployment tested

The YAML below preserves the applied serving spec (images, commands, flags, GPU count, shared memory, media volume, and cache wiring). **Only infrastructure identifiers are redacted**: CPU/GPU pool values, existing PVC name, and cache subpath. Replace those placeholders with your environment's existing values; `hf-token-secret` is only a secret **reference**, never a token value. No cluster name, node identity, IP address, or credential is included.

<details>
<summary>Tested DGD, infrastructure identifiers redacted</summary>

```yaml
apiVersion: nvidia.com/v1beta1
kind: DynamoGraphDeployment
metadata:
  name: vllm-omni-video-agg
spec:
  backendFramework: vllm
  components:
  - name: Frontend
    type: frontend
    replicas: 1
    podTemplate:
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: main
          image: nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/dynamo-frontend:1.4.2
        nodeSelector:
          agentpool: replace-with-cpu-pool
  - name: OmniVideoWorker
    type: worker
    replicas: 1
    sharedMemorySize: 16Gi
    podTemplate:
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: main
          image: nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/vllm-runtime:1.4.2
          command:
          - python3
          - -m
          - dynamo.vllm.omni
          args:
          - --model
          - Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers
          - --output-modalities
          - video
          - --media-output-fs-url
          - file:///tmp/dynamo_media
          - --enforce-eager
          envFrom:
          - secretRef:
              name: hf-token-secret
          resources:
            limits:
              nvidia.com/gpu: '1'
            requests:
              nvidia.com/gpu: '1'
          volumeMounts:
          - name: media-output
            mountPath: /tmp/dynamo_media
          - name: model-cache
            mountPath: /model-cache
            subPath: replace-with-cache-subpath
          env:
          - name: HF_HOME
            value: /model-cache
        volumes:
        - name: media-output
          emptyDir:
            sizeLimit: 40Gi
        - name: model-cache
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: replace-with-model-cache-pvc
        nodeSelector:
          agentpool: replace-with-gpu-pool
```
</details>

## Environment and version verification

Fresh reproduction on **September 10, 2026**, after release alignment:

- Dynamo operator/platform chart: **1.4.2**.
- Frontend: `nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/dynamo-frontend:1.4.2`.
- Worker: `nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/vllm-runtime:1.4.2`.
- Installed in both roles: `ai-dynamo==1.4.2`, `ai-dynamo-runtime==1.4.2`.
- Worker: `vllm==0.26.0`, `vllm-omni==0.26.0rc1`, `torch==2.11.0+cu130`.
- One NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3; driver `580.126.20`; Linux x86_64.
- CPU on the video codec probe: Intel Xeon Platinum 8480C.
- Actual running image identities were compared with fresh public registry manifests, not inferred from tag strings:
  - frontend tag/index digest: `sha256:80589311c904b82927ae95703c1bc59c49eb7ac10d25925c0e457260da915bc7`
  - worker tag/index digest: `sha256:b23ce9e87c413725024ddfd2e06c1e7da220eb48f8a93037f0b01d564b54bd13`

Server-side dry-run, both components' readiness, and `/v1/models` passed. This is a functional reproduction, not a performance benchmark. No source hot-patch or replacement runtime was used for the baseline request.
## Steps to reproduce

1. Save the DGD above as `deployment.yaml`, resolve the placement/cache placeholders, and use an existing namespace, model-cache PVC, and HF secret.
2. Deploy and wait for readiness:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" apply --dry-run=server -f deployment.yaml
   kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" apply -f deployment.yaml
   kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" wait --for=condition=Ready dgd/vllm-omni-video-agg --timeout=20m
   kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" port-forward svc/vllm-omni-video-agg-frontend 8000:8000
   ```

3. In another terminal, confirm `GET /v1/models` contains `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`, then send the request below. The exact saved request was replayed unchanged for the observed September 10 rerun.

Save as `request.json`:

```json
{
  "model": "Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers",
  "prompt": "A dog running on a beach at sunrise",
  "size": "832x480",
  "response_format": "b64_json",
  "nvext": {
    "num_inference_steps": 4,
    "num_frames": 9,
    "seed": 42
  }
}
```

```bash
curl --max-time 1200 -sS -D headers.txt \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/videos \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @request.json -o response.json
```

## Expected behavior

HTTP 200 with `status=completed`, a nonempty `data[0].b64_json` containing the MP4, and decodable video without encoder-introduced magenta/banding. A pod-local filesystem URL is not a remotely usable substitute for explicitly requested base64.

## Actual behavior

HTTP 200 and completed generation, but no `b64_json`. Sanitized response excerpt:

```json
{
  "status": "completed",
  "progress": 100,
  "data": [
    {
      "output_format": "mp4",
      "url": "file:///tmp/dynamo_media/videos/<request-id>.mp4"
    }
  ]
}
```

The forensically recovered MP4 is **27,497 bytes**, decodes to 832×480 video (nine frames, 16 fps), and has severe magenta/banding. The four inference steps are a plumbing smoke test, not a comprehensive model-quality evaluation.

## Diagnosis and suggested scope

### A. Missing per-request field propagation

[`_engine_inputs_from_video()` in the tested release](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/v1.4.2/components/src/dynamo/vllm/omni/omni_handler.py) constructs `EngineInputs` without `response_format=req.response_format`. The [formatter](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/v1.4.2/components/src/dynamo/vllm/omni/output_formatter.py) consequently defaults to `url`.

Static inspection of [current upstream main at `0873e6c52d13`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/0873e6c52d13ebb571b7205b1eda7d523b2d5335/components/src/dynamo/vllm/omni/omni_handler.py) also finds this assignment missing. Current-main serving was not deployed in this rerun.

The direct fix is small:

```diff
 return EngineInputs(
     ...
     request_type=RequestType.VIDEO_GENERATION,
     fps=fps,
+    response_format=req.response_format,
     ...
 )
```

This is an **HTTP request field**, not a launcher CLI flag. The launcher's example `response_format=url` and our intentional Kubernetes `b64_json` request are different delivery choices, not incompatible worker launch flags. A one-line patch was applicability-checked locally, but not deployed as a rebuilt image.

### B. Independent bundled-FFmpeg color defect

The forensically recovered generated MP4 has severe magenta discoloration and horizontal bands. That copy was recovered inside the worker pod; it was **not** successfully delivered to the client as requested base64.

This is not explained by the low inference-step count: a **model-free** synthetic RGB quadrant test reproduces the corruption through both `encode_to_video_bytes()` and `/usr/local/bin/ffmpeg` directly. An independent local FFmpeg decoder reproduces the bad colors.

| Controlled encode path | Result after independent decode |
|---|---|
| Known RGB24 → installed default YUV420p/VP9 path | Magenta/banding |
| Known-good YUV420p → same installed VP9 encoder | Correct colors |
| RGB24 with `-cpuflags mmx+mmxext` | Corruption |
| RGB24 with `-cpuflags mmx` | Correct colors |
| RGB24 with `-cpuflags -mmxext` | Correct colors |
| RGB24 with `-cpuflags 0` | Correct colors |
| RGB24 → YUV444p/VP9 | Correct colors |

The installed FFmpeg reports **8.1.2**, built with `--disable-x86asm`. Its packaged source still unconditionally sets `use_mmx_vfilter=1` in `libswscale/x86/swscale_template.c`; the corresponding external plane writers are gated out. This matches the MMX-filter-layout issue discussed in [FFmpeg's upstream corruption report](https://ffmpeg.org/pipermail/ffmpeg-devel/2024-May/326675.html) and [the upstream guard-fix proposal](https://www.mail-archive.com/ffmpeg-devel@ffmpeg.org/msg184947.html). This report does not assert that the proposal has merged or shipped in a particular FFmpeg release.

<details>
<summary>Model-free codec reproduction used to isolate this defect</summary>

Run in the stock runtime; no GPU model is needed. Decode/inspect the resulting files using an independent, known-good decoder, not just the producer's exit status.

```python
import pathlib
import subprocess
import numpy as np
from dynamo.common.utils.video_utils import encode_to_video_bytes

out = pathlib.Path('/tmp/dynamo-codec-repro')
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
frame = np.zeros((480, 832, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
frame[:240, :416] = [255, 0, 0]
frame[:240, 416:] = [0, 255, 0]
frame[240:, :416] = [0, 0, 255]
frame[240:, 416:] = [255, 255, 255]
frames = np.stack([frame] * 9)
(out / 'dynamo.mp4').write_bytes(
    encode_to_video_bytes(frames, fps=16, output_format='mp4')
)
for label, flags in [('default', []), ('no-mmxext', ['-cpuflags', '-mmxext'])]:
    subprocess.run([
        '/usr/local/bin/ffmpeg', '-y', '-hide_banner', '-loglevel', 'error',
        *flags, '-f', 'rawvideo', '-pix_fmt', 'rgb24', '-s', '832x480',
        '-r', '16', '-i', 'pipe:0', '-an', '-c:v', 'libvpx-vp9',
        '-pix_fmt', 'yuv420p', str(out / f'{label}.mp4'),
    ], input=frames.tobytes(), check=True)
```

The default red quadrant decodes approximately magenta (`255,0,255`); the MMXEXT-disabled control decodes approximately red (`252,0,0`). The exact corrupted bytes vary; pixel correctness is the assertion.
</details>

Disabling MMXEXT is a **diagnostic workaround**, not a performance-qualified deployment fix. Backport/validate the FFmpeg guard fix (or another correct build configuration) in a rebuilt runtime and add an RGB→video→RGB regression. No patched end-to-end model run was performed in this investigation.
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The video handler preserves explicit `response_format=b64_json` and returns a decodable inline MP4 without requiring pod access.
- [ ] Explicit URL delivery remains correct when externally served media storage is configured.
- [ ] The shipped runtime passes a model-free RGB-quadrant color round-trip, including the relevant x86 build configuration.
- [ ] The corresponding DGD request passes against rebuilt, version-identified images.
- [ ] A sensible-step generation is visually checked after the transport/codec fixes; the four-step smoke is not treated as a quality approval.

## Validation boundary and cleanup

Only the stated stock-release failure and diagnostic comparisons have been verified. No patched end-to-end deployment is claimed. Temporary test DGDs were removed after capture; source/example code and shared controllers were not changed. Full local manifests, requests, redacted logs, runtime sources, media, hashes, and cleanup evidence were retained; private cluster diagnostics are intentionally not pasted into this public issue.

## Related case trackers

- #14667: `vllm-omni-video-agg`
- #14668: `vllm-omni-i2v-agg`
- #14669: `vllm-omni-audio-agg`

T2V and I2V share the field-propagation and codec root causes; these separate issues track each example's end-to-end qualification, not unrelated implementations of the same fix. Parent documentation/qualification tracker: #13383.

title: DEP: Cross-replica PolicyClass fairness contract
body:
## Summary

PolicyClass weighted scheduling currently has process-local queue and deficit
state. When forwarding replicas share eligible worker capacity, uneven ingress
can change the aggregate scheduling-cost share received by each PolicyClass.

This draft requests feedback on whether Dynamo should define an aggregate
cross-replica PolicyClass fairness invariant, and if so, on the scheduling-domain
boundary and an appropriate first implementation scope. It does not request
approval of an implementation.

## Motivation

PolicyClass uses per-class queue state and deficit-round-robin accounting.
`--router-replica-sync` synchronizes active-sequence lifecycle state but does not
replicate PolicyClass queues, DRR deficits, or the scheduling ring cursor.

A local two-frontend reproduction with one shared CPU Mocker worker, identical
worker eligibility, 512-token cache-distinct equal-cost prompts, a 4:1
`premium:regular` policy, and replica sync enabled observed:

| Topology and ingress | Premium cost | Regular cost | Equivalent requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| One router, balanced | 130560 | 33280 | 255:65 |
| Two routers, balanced | 133120 | 34304 | 260:67 |
| Two routers, direct skew | 83456 | 82944 | 163:162 |
| Two routers, swapped skew | 82944 | 83456 | 162:163 |

Direct skew sends `premium` requests only to router A and `regular` requests
only to router B. Swapped skew reverses that placement: `premium` goes only to
router B and `regular` only to router A.

The results use cumulative successful-booking scheduling-cost counters. The
sampler starts at an aggregate target of 320 equal-cost bookings; because it
polls Prometheus, it can include several bookings that arrive between scrapes.
The table therefore reports the observed bounded window, not a claim of an exact
320th-booking cut. Balanced ingress remains near 4:1, while either skewed
placement is near 1:1. Swapping class placement reverses the small residual.

## Proposal

Define the desired PolicyClass contract for continuously backlogged classes that
compete for the same scheduling domain and eligible, work-conserving capacity.
If Dynamo supports aggregate cross-replica fairness, specify a scheduling-cost
share bound that is independent of ingress placement and accounts for the
maximum booked request cost and finite observation window.

This DEP does not propose global strict ordering, fairness between classes with
different eligible worker sets, or PolicyClass as an authentication boundary.

A candidate Phase 1 is one logical scheduling owner per scheduling domain.
Forwarding replicas would resolve the class, send admission intent to the owner,
and forward work selected by the owner. This is a candidate only; a standalone
owner, a designated router owner, bounded approximate coordination, and explicit
local-only semantics remain open alternatives.

## Alternate Solutions

### Keep independent local schedulers

Preserves current availability and avoids an additional admission hop, while
documenting that weighted fairness is local to each router process.

### One logical scheduling owner

Provides one PolicyClass queue and one DRR budget per scheduling domain, at the
cost of an admission hop and explicit availability semantics.

### Sharded owners

Assigns domains deterministically across owners without splitting a domain's
queue or budget. Rebalancing and skew management would be follow-up work.

### Approximate replicated budgets

May avoid centralization, but needs explicit reconciliation and an error bound
before it can satisfy an aggregate-share contract.

## Requirements

- State whether PolicyClass fairness is local-only or has a supported aggregate
  cross-replica scheduling-cost bound.
- Scope any aggregate contract to a defined scheduling domain and shared worker
  eligibility set.
- Use successful-booking scheduling-cost units, not HTTP completion order, for
  acceptance evidence.
- If a global contract is selected, add a deterministic one-versus-many
  frontend regression test with balanced, direct-skew, and swapped-skew ingress.
- Replace the current Prometheus-polling observation with exact fixed-booking
  window capture before treating the reproducer as durable regression coverage.

## Open Questions

1. Should aggregate cross-replica PolicyClass fairness be a supported invariant,
   or should the product explicitly retain local-only fairness semantics?
2. If supported, what defines the scheduling domain and eligibility boundary?
3. Is one logical scheduling owner an acceptable Phase 1 direction, or is a
   bounded distributed protocol preferred?
4. Which router boundary should own a deterministic multi-replica reproducer and
   its observability?

## References

- PolicyClass single-router prioritization: #12465
- Shared SelectionCore DEP: #14310
- Worker-taint synchronization DEP: #12050
- Experiment instrumentation commit:
  https://github.com/tryambak2019/dynamo/commit/6fb6b7029ea7b5722918fd27a2c09aea61ad99ae
- PolicyClass configuration documentation:
  https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/latest/knowledge-base/modular-components/router/configuration-and-tuning#policy-class-queues

Kubernetes 1.34.11

The metric we use for scale-up from zero is `dynamo_pending_request` in the ScaledObjects YAML and that's a custom metric Open WebUI emits when a model needs to scale up.

title: nixl build_and_deploy.sh silently exits when an invalid architecture is entered instead of retrying
body:
## Describe the Bug

`deploy/pre-deployment/nixl/build_and_deploy.sh` prompts for an architecture
and is meant to reject an invalid answer with `Error: Invalid architecture.
Please select 1, 2, x86_64, or aarch64` and loop back to re-prompt — that
message and the surrounding `while true` retry loop exist specifically for
this. Instead, any invalid answer silently kills the whole script.

The prompt assigns the validator's result as a bare
`SELECTED_ARCH=$(validate_architecture "$arch_input")` statement and only
afterward checks `$?`. The script runs under `set -euo pipefail`. A bare
assignment whose command substitution returns non-zero is not exempt from
`-e` (unlike the same check written directly as an `if` condition, which the
rest of this file already uses correctly — e.g. `if ! command_exists wget`),
so the moment `validate_architecture` returns 1 for an invalid answer, the
shell exits immediately, before the `if [ $? -eq 0 ]` check, the error
message, and the retry loop ever run.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `cd deploy/pre-deployment/nixl && ./build_and_deploy.sh` (with `wget`,
   `unzip`, `kubectl`, `docker` on `PATH` so the dependency check passes).
2. At `Select architecture (1-2 or enter x86_64/aarch64):`, type anything
   other than exactly `1`, `2`, `x86_64`, or `aarch64` (e.g. a typo like
   `x86`).

## Expected Behavior

`Error: Invalid architecture. Please select 1, 2, x86_64, or aarch64` is
printed and the prompt repeats.

## Actual Behavior

The script exits immediately with status 1 and no message at all — the
retry error text never appears.

```
$ printf 'not-a-real-arch\n' | ./build_and_deploy.sh
...
Select architecture (1-2 or enter x86_64/aarch64):
$ echo $?
1
```

## Environment

Bash 5.2.21, Linux x86_64. Reproduces under any bash implementing POSIX
`set -e` semantics for a plain command-substitution assignment — not
version-specific.


- `num_input_tokens` is the same quantity the router matches against (`request.token_ids.len()`), so the report will be accepted.
- `output.request_perf_metrics` is already consulted for timing; if the installed TRT-LLM exposes `kv_cache_metrics` (reused / missed / newly allocated blocks), it can cross-check `cached_tokens` and would give an exact reused-block count — optional.

title: fix(router): per-model and per-pool separation for the router's per-attempt metrics
body:
## Summary

`RouterRequestMetrics::from_component` (`lib/llm/src/kv_router/metrics.rs`) is memoised in a process-global `static OnceLock`. Its `router_id` label is the DRT `instance_id` of whichever component initialised it first. Routing hosts are created per model endpoint and per pool (prefill / decode), but every one of them in a process shares that single instance. As a result `router_input_sequence_tokens`, `router_output_sequence_tokens`, `router_kv_hit_rate`, `router_time_to_first_token_seconds` and `router_inter_token_latency_seconds` merge all models and both pools of a frontend into one series each. This is also the only reason `router_overlap_blocks_lost` needed its own `worker_type` label.

The new KV-cache reuse series from #14103 (with the labels proposed in its review) carry `phase` and `model`; the rest of the per-attempt family does not.

## Options

1. **Labels.** Add `phase` (`aggregated | prefill | decode`, from `tracker.phase()`, already the label used by `stage_duration_seconds`) and `model` (`PreprocessedRequest.model`, a closed set) to the remaining per-attempt series. Additive; existing dashboards keep their meaning with `sum without (phase, model)`.
2. **Root cause.** Make `RouterRequestMetrics` per component instead of per process, so `router_id` identifies the model endpoint. The static accessor `RouterRequestMetrics::get()` has two callers (`kv_router/scheduler.rs`, `kv_router.rs`) that would need the instance passed in.

Option 2 is cleaner; option 1 is smaller and can be done first.

## Acceptance

A single frontend serving two models in disaggregated mode exports distinguishable per-attempt series for each model and each pool; the catalog's "compare within a pool" guidance becomes true within one process.

Related: #14103, #15173.

title: fix(operator): deprecate unrestricted WithSharedOwnership
body:
## Summary

`WithSharedOwnership` bypasses controller-owner validation for an existing same-named resource. It does not verify that the existing controller owner belongs to the intended lifecycle.

It currently supports two different resource lifecycles: a model-scoped HeadlessService and a checkpoint Job DRA `ResourceClaimTemplate` (RCT). Neither is unrestricted shared ownership.

`WithSharedOwnership` should be deprecated. It cannot establish that an existing resource belongs to the intended lifecycle, so new lifecycle implementations must not depend on it.

## Current layouts

### Model HeadlessService

`ReconcileModelServicesForComponents` creates one deterministic Service per `(namespace, baseModelName)`.

```text
DGD A, model-A
  └── HeadlessService(model-A), controller owner = DGD A

DGD B, model-A
  └── reconciles that same Service with WithSharedOwnership
```

The Service selects all pods serving `model-A` and produces EndpointSlices consumed by `DynamoModel` endpoint discovery.

Problems:

- The first DGD/DCD becomes the sole controller owner of a model-scoped resource.
- Deleting that owner can garbage-collect the Service while other DGDs/DCDs still serve the base model.
- A later reconciler accepts an ownerless Service or one controlled by an unrelated object, provided its name and namespace collide.
- Multiple controller owner references are not an appropriate solution: the Service should have one controller owner.

Relevant source: `deploy/operator/internal/dynamo/model_service.go`.

### Checkpoint GMS/DRA ResourceClaimTemplate

A DGD-managed checkpoint creates a separate RCT for its checkpoint Job:

```text
DGD serving workload RCT:
  chat-worker-gpu
  controller owner = DGD

Checkpoint Job RCT:
  checkpoint-<checkpointID>-worker-gpu
  initial controller owner = DGD
  final controller owner = DynamoCheckpoint
```

Current sequence:

1. The DGD derives GPU count and DeviceClass from the component.
2. It creates the checkpoint RCT with itself as parent.
3. It prepares the checkpoint Job pod template to reference that RCT.
4. It creates or finds the automatic `DynamoCheckpoint`.
5. It transfers the RCT controller owner to the `DynamoCheckpoint`.
6. Subsequent DGD reconciles use `WithSharedOwnership` to access the now-checkpoint-owned RCT.

Problems:

- This is an ownership handoff, not shared ownership.
- The DGD reconcile can operate on an arbitrary same-named RCT rather than the expected checkpoint-owned one.
- The handoff exists because the DGD currently prepares the checkpoint pod template before creating the checkpoint CR.

Relevant source: `deploy/operator/internal/controller/dgd_checkpoints_reconciler.go`.

## Proposed resolution

### Model HeadlessService lifecycle

Move the Service under one model-scoped controller owner.

Options:

1. Introduce a dedicated model-service/base-model CR keyed by `(namespace, baseModelName)`. It owns the HeadlessService.
2. Formalize one canonical `DynamoModel` with `modelType: base` per `(namespace, baseModelName)` and make it own the Service. This requires deterministic identity plus uniqueness/conflict handling; today `base` is only a supported type, not an enforced singleton.

DGD/DCD components then contribute selected pods only. LoRA `DynamoModel`s discover the EndpointSlices but do not own the Service.

Do not solve this with multiple controller owner references.

### Checkpoint RCT lifecycle

Preferred: move checkpoint-RCT creation into `DynamoCheckpointReconciler`.

```text
DGD
  └── creates DynamoCheckpoint with checkpoint DRA inputs

DynamoCheckpoint controller
  ├── creates/updates checkpoint RCT, parent = DynamoCheckpoint
  └── renders checkpoint Job with its deterministic RCT reference
```

This removes the DGD-to-checkpoint owner transfer and the `WithSharedOwnership` call.

The `DynamoCheckpoint` API/controller must retain or explicitly carry the input needed to render the RCT—GPU count and DeviceClass—before DRA preparation removes scalar GPU resources from the pod template.

A smaller alternative is an explicit, exact DGD-to-`DynamoCheckpoint` handoff policy. It must validate the deterministic checkpoint identity and must not permit arbitrary RCT ownership.

## Acceptance criteria

- `WithSharedOwnership` is deprecated, and both lifecycle implementations no longer require it.
- The model HeadlessService has one model-scoped lifecycle owner, independent of which DGD/DCD first served the model.
- A checkpoint RCT has `DynamoCheckpoint` as its controller owner throughout its durable lifecycle.
- Tests cover ownerless and foreign-controller resources, expected lifecycle ownership, stale/recreated owner UID, and delete behavior.

## References

- Follow-up to #13474.
- Replacement PR: #13990.

title: DEP: Production hardening for persistent GMS KV failover
body:
## Summary

Harden persistent GMS KV failover for vLLM and SGLang after their engine-specific MVPs. This train keeps inference-engine scheduling, hashes, cache indexes, and eviction policy native to each engine. GMS owns daemon-lifetime GPU allocations plus generation-fenced recovery metadata.

All implementation PRs remain drafts. On 2026-09-22 the existing PRs were updated in place, preserving their discussion history, and the complete stack was rebased onto Dynamo main at `2e4998a30ccd6298d81c4263a49b6fa9a0b273c6`.

Parent engine trackers: #12053 (vLLM) and #14704 (SGLang). Recovery-strategy discussion: #14828.

## Architecture

```text
engine-native allocator and prefix index
              |
engine adapter: transactional publish/adopt
              |
generation-fenced content directory
              |
block validity, TP agreement, writer retirement
              |
daemon-owned persistent GPU allocation (v0 or v1)
```

There is one serving owner. A replacement may reuse exact-generation sealed KV after writer retirement and safe classification. Ambiguous predecessor accesses remain quarantined unless a separately qualified GPU-quiescence provider proves they can be reclaimed. Process death, heartbeats, traffic silence, and fixed delays are not treated as CUDA-quiescence proof.

## Prerequisite backend PRs

| PR | Outcome |
|---|---|
| #14814 | Persistent-pool backend contract and v0 implementation |
| #14818 | Persistent pools through the v1 backend |

## Hardening review order

| Step | Draft PR | Outcome |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | #15036 | Startup verification, bounded vLLM promotion, and TP-compatible reattachment |
| 2 | #15037 | Service fencing, lifecycle-aware acceptance, and amortized SGLang coordination |
| 3 | #15038 | Ordered directory work and bounded SGLang pressure |
| 4 | #15039 | Generation-safe reads and transactional engine recovery state |
| 5 | #15040 | SGLang ownership preservation and bounded request continuity |
| 6 | #15041 | Review hardening, standby headroom, and orphaned-rank fail-stop |
| 7 | #15042 | Repository validation and stale-writer rejection |
| 8 | #15043 | Fail-closed quarantine separated from optional GPU quiescence |
| 9 | #15044 | Retryable vLLM KV and SGLang crash headroom |
| 10 | #15045 | TP rank fail-stop and prompt failure broadcast |
| 11 | #15046 | Warm mappings, lease-safe stabilization, and classify-before-admission |
| 12 | #15047 | Interrupted-request replay and dead-cohort latency |
| 13 | #15048 | Shadow prewarm and completed-KV journaling |
| 14 | #15049 | Runtime contract fixes and native-route test alignment |
| 15 | #15050 | Writer-authority publication guard and final cleanup |

Final public tip: `61bd54806517debf97da4ca432a3397b87c065b8`.

## Safety boundary

The earlier vLLM and SGLang checkpoints demonstrate the engine integrations and controlled crash loop. The complete arbitrary-crash safety model is cumulative through this hardening train. Reviewers should not infer final quarantine or writer-retirement guarantees from an earlier engine-only checkpoint.

Required invariants:

- Never serve a directory record whose slot generation is stale.
- Never admit a replacement writer before predecessor writers are retired and predecessor KV is classified.
- Require TP ranks to agree before allocation, adoption, reclamation, or takeover succeeds.
- Treat malformed, missing, reordered, or incompatible recovery metadata as a miss or startup failure.
- Keep directory and TP coordination off the per-token hot path.
- Preserve engine-native capacity, free-list, refcount, and rollback semantics.

## Scope

Included: local persistent HBM, vLLM/SGLang integration, TP recovery coordination, request continuity, v0/v1 pool backends, and failover hardening.

Excluded: KVCR tiering, host/storage tiers, remote transfer, router-directed P2P, decode-to-decode transfer, TensorRT-LLM, node/GPU-reset durability, and authenticated same-user multi-tenancy.

## Validation status

The remapped public tree preserves the locally reviewed simplified implementation and adds only repository-required isort/Black formatting; all 43 public PRs remain non-empty. Existing review comments and PR identities were preserved. Previous public heads are retained under local archive refs.

Per-PR CI and focused correctness checks must be rerun after the restack. Fresh TTFT, ITL, throughput, large-model, and Kubernetes qualification is intentionally deferred and must not be inferred from pre-restack measurements.

title: [BUG]: DGDR hardware auto-discovery writes the raw nvidia.com/gpu.product string into spec.hardware.gpuSku, which its own CRD enum then rejects
body:
## Describe the Bug

DGDR hardware auto-discovery can write a value into `spec.hardware.gpuSku` that its own CRD
enum rejects, so the reconcile fails and the DGDR never progresses.

`InferHardwareSystem` in `deploy/operator/internal/gpu/discovery.go` is careful here — its
doc comment states that unknown GPUs "gracefully return empty string", and it does:

```go
// Matching is based on substring checks and is tolerant of variations
// in formatting (case, spaces, dashes). If no known GPU is detected,
// an empty SKU type is returned.
```

But the caller in `enrichHardwareFromDiscovery`
(`deploy/operator/internal/controller/dynamographdeploymentrequest_controller.go`) discards
that guarantee and falls back to the raw product string:

```go
	if hw.GPUSKU == "" {
		inferred := gpu.InferHardwareSystem(gpuInfo.Model)
		switch {
		case gpuInfo.System != "":
			hw.GPUSKU = gpuInfo.System
		case inferred != "":
			hw.GPUSKU = inferred
		default:
			hw.GPUSKU = nvidiacomv1beta1.GPUSKUType(gpuInfo.Model)   // <-- raw label value
		}
		changed = true
	}
```

`gpuInfo.Model` comes from the `nvidia.com/gpu.product` node label
(`LabelGPUProduct` in the same discovery package). That string is free-form and is
**guaranteed not to be a member of the enum** whenever `InferHardwareSystem` returned empty —
because "returned empty" means precisely "this product string matched none of the known
tokens".

`HardwareSpec.GPUSKU` is validated by:

```go
	// +kubebuilder:validation:Enum=gb200_sxm;gb10;b200_sxm;h200_sxm;h100_sxm;h100_pcie;a100_sxm;a100_pcie;a30;l40s;l40;l4;v100_sxm;v100_pcie;t4;mi200;mi300
	GPUSKU GPUSKUType `json:"gpuSku,omitempty"`
```

So the subsequent `r.Update(ctx, dgdr)` in `createProfilingJob` is rejected by the API server
and the reconcile returns `failed to update DGDR with auto-discovered hardware`.

The net effect: **on any GPU model the enum does not list, DGDR auto-discovery fails with a
validation error rather than degrading gracefully** — even though the discovery helper was
written to degrade gracefully.

This code is identical on `v1.3.1` and on `main` as of 2026-08-14.

**Update (2026-08-14): the enum is not derived from AIConfigurator's system list, and the perf
data for this GPU already exists upstream.** `aiconfigurator` ships a system definition and a
full kernel database for this exact part:

- `aic-core/src/aiconfigurator_core/systems/rtx_pro_6000_server.yaml` — measured on a real
  node (`mem_capacity: 102641958912` = 97887 MiB, `sm_version: 120`, `power: 600`,
  `num_gpus_per_node: 8`, comment notes collection on 2026-07-25)
- `systems/data/rtx_pro_6000_server/` — attention, gemm, moe, mla, mla_bmm, comm,
  linear_attention, encoder_attention, kda, mhc
- `systems/support_matrix/rtx_pro_6000_server.csv` — 1013 rows of validated
  model x backend x version x mode combinations, e.g. `vllm 0.19.0 agg -> PASS (silicon)`
  and `trtllm 1.3.0rc20 disagg -> PASS (silicon)`

Comparing the CRD enum (17 values) against `aiconfigurator`'s systems directory (14 systems),
the two diverge in **both** directions:

| | values |
|---|---|
| In AIC, missing from the enum | `rtx_pro_6000_server`, `b300_sxm`, `b60`, `gb300` (plus `gb200`, which the enum spells `gb200_sxm`) |
| In the enum, no AIC system | `gb10`, `l40`, `t4`, `v100_sxm`, `v100_pcie`, `mi200`, `mi300` |
| Present in both | `a100_pcie`, `a100_sxm`, `a30`, `b200_sxm`, `h100_pcie`, `h100_sxm`, `h200_sxm`, `l4`, `l40s` |

So only 9 of the 17 accepted values correspond to a system the profiler actually has data for.
That suggests the enum should be generated from (or validated against) AIC's systems list
rather than maintained separately.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run on a cluster whose GPU nodes carry a `nvidia.com/gpu.product` label that
   `InferHardwareSystem` does not match. Ours is:

   ```
   nvidia.com/gpu.product: NVIDIA-RTX-PRO-6000-Blackwell-Server-Edition
   ```

2. Apply a `DynamoGraphDeploymentRequest` **without** `spec.hardware` (or with any of
   `gpuSku`/`vramMb`/`numGpusPerNode`/`totalGpus` omitted, which triggers discovery).

3. Watch the operator log / DGDR status.

## Expected Behavior

Auto-discovery either leaves `gpuSku` empty and reports a clear, actionable message naming the
unrecognised product string and the accepted values, or the enum covers the GPU. In no case
should the operator write a value it will then reject itself.

A minimal fix would be to drop the `default:` branch — leaving `hw.GPUSKU` empty and surfacing
"could not infer gpuSku from node label %q; set spec.hardware.gpuSku explicitly" — so the
failure names the actual problem.

## Actual Behavior

```
failed to update DGDR with auto-discovered hardware:
  spec.hardware.gpuSku: Unsupported value: "NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition"
  supported values: gb200_sxm, gb10, b200_sxm, h200_sxm, h100_sxm, h100_pcie,
                    a100_sxm, a100_pcie, a30, l40s, l40, l4, v100_sxm, v100_pcie,
                    t4, mi200, mi300
```

The message reads as "you supplied a bad value", but we supplied nothing — the operator
discovered it, wrote it, and rejected it. That made this take longer to diagnose than it
should have.

## Environment

- Dynamo operator **1.3.1**; DGDR CRD storage version `nvidia.com/v1beta1`
  (code re-checked against `main` on 2026-08-14)
- `dynamo env` output is not applicable here: there is no local Dynamo install involved. The
  defect is in the operator's reconcile loop, reached by applying a DGDR to the cluster.
- Kubernetes **v1.35.6** (vanilla), managed by NVIDIA Run:ai 2.26.27
- GPUs: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), 96 GiB, 8 per node
- `nvidia.com/gpu.product` = `NVIDIA-RTX-PRO-6000-Blackwell-Server-Edition`

## Additional Context

- **Workaround**: set all four `spec.hardware` fields explicitly, which skips discovery
  entirely (the `HardwareSpec` doc comment documents this: "If all four fields are set,
  discovery is skipped"). We use `gpuSku: l40s` as the nearest listed GDDR part so the
  operator accepts the DGDR.

- **The workaround has a real cost, which is why this matters beyond the error message.**
  `gpuSku` is what the profiler keys its performance data on, and the value we are forced to
  pick is a different GPU. Observed on 2026-08-14 with `gpuSku: l40s`, `searchStrategy: rapid`
  and `features.mocker`:

  ```
  perf_database.get_database: Loading database for system='l40s', backend='vllm',
                              version='0.14.0'
  task.run: Starting Pareto Analysis for
            disagg_Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B_l40s_None_vllm_0.14.0_512_256_0_200.0_10.0
  profile_sla._execute_strategy: Selected prefill: tp1 (1 GPUs), decode: tp2 (2 GPUs)
  profile_sla.run_profile: Final cleanup completed.
  ```

  Profiling **succeeds silently** against L40S data (48 GB GDDR6, Ada) for a 96 GB GDDR7
  SM120 part, and the resulting parallelism plan is not meaningful for this hardware. No
  warning is emitted that the requested hardware is not the hardware being modelled. An

title: [BUG]: KVBM disk→device onboarding silently serves the wrong KV when the GDS_MT file registration fails (no nvidia-fs); kvbm 1.4.2 + vLLM 0.27.1 standalone connector
body:
### Describe the Bug

With the standalone `kvbm==1.4.2` wheel and vLLM 0.27.1 (`DynamoConnector`, `kv_role=kv_both`, host + disk tiers), a request whose blocks are onboarded from the **disk** tier is served with the **wrong KV cache** — the model answers with the content of the previous (evicting) request — and no error is returned to the client. KVBM's own metrics report a full hit (`kvbm_onboard_blocks_d2d` == every block of the prompt) while the transfer actually failed:

```
E gds_mt_backend.cpp:237] GDS_MT: failed to create file handle: GDS_MT: file register error: error=5027, fd=149   (at startup)
E nixl_agent.cpp:921] createXferReq: no specified or potential backend had the required registrations to be able to do the transfer
ERROR dynamo_llm::block_manager::distributed::transfer: Failed to write to blocks: Other(Failed to create XferRequest)
ERROR dynamo_llm::block_manager::distributed::transfer: Batched connector transfer failed: Failed to create XferRequest
ERROR dynamo_runtime::utils::tasks::critical: Critical task 'ZmqActiveMessageWorker: Handler for function: transfer_blocks' failed: Failed to create XferRequest
```

After that, the engine sits at `Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs, Deferred: 1 reqs` for minutes (`got a finished warning for a request that is onboarding`) while `/health` still returns 200.

The machine has no `nvidia-fs` kernel module (GB10 / sm_121 aarch64 workstation with unified memory), so cuFile cannot register the disk-cache file. That is an environment limitation; the bug is that (a) `build_agent(worker_id, need_disk)` in `lib/llm/src/block_manager/distributed/worker.rs` always creates the GDS_MT backend and the planner uses the direct disk→device path even when the registration failed, without falling back to the POSIX/host two-hop path, and (b) the failed `transfer_blocks` is not propagated to the connector/vLLM, so the blocks are handed to the scheduler as loaded and the physical GPU blocks still contain the previous request's KV.

The same error string appears in #5012 (closed stale) and in the follow-up reports in #5857.

### Steps to Reproduce

Container `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1-aarch64-ubuntu2404` (vLLM 0.27.1, torch 2.13 cu130, NIXL 1.3.1), then inside it:

```bash
pip install --no-deps kvbm==1.4.2     # plain `pip install kvbm` pulls nixl==1.0.1 and breaks vLLM's nixl_ep import

export DYN_KVBM_CPU_CACHE_GB=8 DYN_KVBM_DISK_CACHE_GB=64 DYN_KVBM_DISK_CACHE_DIR=/kvbm-disk \
       DYN_KVBM_DISABLE_DISK_OFFLOAD_FILTER=true DYN_KVBM_METRICS=true DYN_KVBM_METRICS_PORT=6880

vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --served-model-name qwen3-8b --port 8000 \
  --max-model-len 40960 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.20 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"DynamoConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_module_path":"kvbm.vllm_integration.connector"}'
```

GPU KV pool in this configuration: 44,832 tokens.

Probe (temperature 0, thinking disabled, streaming):
1. Send document A (~30K tokens, "[doc 1000] <random code words>… Question: what is the first code word?"). Answer: `yankee` (correct). TTFT 9.0 s.
2. Send four different ~30K-token documents E1–E4 to evict A from the GPU pool and from the 8 GB host tier (last one, E4, answers `delta`).
3. Send document A again.

Full probe script (calibrates tokens/word, checks the expected word, diffs `kvbm_*` counters): https://github.com/ryangu00/dell-pro-max-gb10-kvbm-ssd-kv-cache/blob/main/scripts/kvbm_probe.py

### Expected Behavior

Either A is served from disk with the correct KV (answer `yankee`), or KVBM reports a miss / raises and vLLM recomputes the prefill.

### Actual Behavior

Step 3 returns in 0.22 s with the answer `delta` (E4's answer). Metrics delta between step 1 and step 3: `kvbm_onboard_blocks_d2d` +1884 (= 30,156 tokens / 16), `kvbm_offload_blocks_d2h` +7536, `kvbm_offload_blocks_h2d` +7536. Engine log shows the `createXferReq` failure above at the moment of the "hit".

Controls on the same machine and model:
- No KVBM: step 3 TTFT 9.13 s, answer `yankee` (recompute, correct).
- KVBM with host tier only (no `DYN_KVBM_DISK_CACHE_GB`), evict 1: step 3 TTFT 0.25 s, answer `yankee`, `kvbm_onboard_blocks_h2d` +971 — host→device onboarding is correct.
- Setting `DYN_KVBM_NIXL_BACKEND_POSIX=true` / `DYN_KVBM_NIXL_BACKEND_GDS_MT=false` / `DYN_KVBM_NIXL_BACKEND_GDS=false`, and separately a cuFile `force_compat_mode` config via `CUFILE_ENV_PATH_JSON`, reproduce the identical failure.

Raw probe JSON and engine logs for every run: https://github.com/ryangu00/dell-pro-max-gb10-kvbm-ssd-kv-cache/tree/main/results

### Environment

- Dynamo / KVBM: `kvbm==1.4.2` (PyPI aarch64 wheel), used standalone via `vllm serve --kv-transfer-config`
- vLLM 0.27.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130, NIXL 1.3.1 (image's own), Python 3.12
- Driver 580.142, CUDA 13; no `nvidia-fs` module
- Hardware: single GB10 (Dell Pro Max with GB10), 128 GB unified memory, sm_121, aarch64, NVMe ext4 for the disk cache
- Model: Qwen/Qwen3-8B (dense; hybrid models fail earlier with `Failed to promote local KV cache specs to one unified type`, tracked separately in #8051)

### Suggested behavior

1. If GDS_MT file registration fails at startup, either fail the disk tier loudly or fall back to the host-bounce (POSIX) path for disk↔device.
2. A failed `transfer_blocks` must mark the request's blocks as not loaded (or fail the request) instead of leaving the scheduler with stale physical blocks.

title: [FEATURE]: Shared-cache tier for the vLLM MooncakeStoreConnector (--shared-cache-type mooncake-store)
body:
### Feature request

Add a shared-cache tier implementation for the vLLM `MooncakeStoreConnector`, e.g. `--shared-cache-type mooncake-store` (a `VllmMooncakeStore` next to `HicacheSharedKvCache`), so the KV router can see blocks that live only in the shared Mooncake store when the engine is vLLM.

Today `--shared-cache-type hicache` (`lib/llm/src/kv_router/shared_cache.rs`) consumes the Mooncake master's KV-event stream (`ENABLE_KV_EVENTS`, ZMQ PUB of `stored` / `removed` per object) but derives keys with SGLang's HiCache scheme (`{sha256 page hash}_{rank}_k/v` from the `sglang_hicache_mooncake` model card). With a vLLM worker it is inert: the vLLM connector's object keys look like

```
{cache_prefix}@{model}{namespace}@tp_rank:R@pcp0@dcp{D}@pp_rank:0@group:{G}@{chunk_hash_hex}
```

with one Mooncake `group_id` per chunk (`vllm-mooncake-store:{cache_prefix}@{model}{namespace}@{chunk_hash_hex}`) shared by the per-rank / per-KV-group objects, so nothing the hicache client computes ever matches.

### Describe the problem you're encountering

Setup: vLLM main (post vllm#55531) with `MooncakeStoreConnector` as the L3 in a `MultiConnector`, PD disaggregated on GB300 (TP4 / DCP4, hybrid MLA + linear-attention model with two prefix-cacheable KV cache groups), Dynamo frontend at `202478991b`, Mooncake `0.3.13+gb46235d` built from source with `-DENABLE_KV_EVENTS=ON`.

The router indexes only the workers' GPU-tier KV events. The connector's own store events arrive with `medium="cpu"` (lowercase) and are dropped by `StorageTier::from_kv_medium`, which is arguably correct since they describe a rack-shared pool, not the publishing worker's host tier. The result is that a prefix that is fully present in the shared store is scored as cold, so worker selection ignores L3 locality and, for anyone using booked prefill tokens for admission, the request is booked as a full cold prefill.

Points that shaped the design we ended up with, in case they help whoever picks this up:

- vLLM's chunk hash is sha256 over a pickled `(parent_hash, tokens, extra_keys)` chained from a process-seeded `NONE_HASH`, so the router cannot recompute the keys from tokens the way the hicache client does. But the workers' GPU `stored` events already carry the exact chain: `KvCacheStoredBlockData { block_hash (external, u64 = low 64 bits of the chunk hash), tokens_hash }` plus `parent_hash`. Learning a `(parent_external, tokens_hash) -> external` map from those events, tapped in `Indexer::try_apply_event` before the radix tree's parent check (so events rejected as `parent_block_not_found` still teach the chain), gives router-granularity keys with zero dependence on vLLM's pickle format.
- Presence can be keyed by the chunk hash parsed from the event's `group_id` (trailing hex after the last `@`) rather than `object_key`, which collapses the `dcp × groups` objects of one chunk into one entry. A `removed` for the group should drop the chunk (the engine needs every rank namespace present, so a partial chunk must read as a miss). A sequence gap or subscriber reconnect should clear presence but keep the learned chain.
- Lookup then walks the chain over the request's per-block `LocalBlockHash`es and returns the prefix run, since the connector can only extend a prefix.
- The chain map needs a bound that fits real stores (the existing `MAX_MOONCAKE_INDEX_ENTRIES` of 1,000,000 is far below a multi-TB store's key count); a two-generation sweep works.
- Useful extra metrics: present entries, chain entries, and blocks that stopped on a missing chain link rather than an absent hash (tells whether learning coverage is the bottleneck).
- Mooncake side: the publisher is a compile-time option that upstream defaults off, and its `dependencies.sh` only installs libzmq on the Debian/Ubuntu branch, so a manylinux (AlmaLinux) wheel build needs `zeromq-devel` added by hand before configure.

### Describe alternatives you've tried

- `--shared-cache-type hicache` against the vLLM connector: inert, as above.
- Admitting the connector's lowercase `cpu` events as a host tier: wrong, it would credit rack-shared blocks as host residency of one worker and double count against the disk weight.
- We implemented the approach above as a patch on our frontend build (new `SharedCacheType::MooncakeStore`, `SharedKvCache::observe_stored` / `check_blocks_by_local_hashes` trait additions, `Arc<dyn SharedKvCache>` shared between the router and the indexer), and it passes the kv-router and dynamo-llm test suites. Happy to share it as a reference for whoever takes this upstream; a native implementation would let us drop the patch.

title: dynamo.frontend Config::Triton metadata drops max_batch_size, KServe v2 clients get shape mismatch on batchable models
body:
## Summary

In `lib/llm/src/grpc/service/kserve.rs`, the `Config::Triton` branch of `model_metadata()` reports tensor `shape` verbatim from `model_config.input.dims`, without prepending a batch dimension when `max_batch_size > 0`. Native Triton's KServe adapter adds `-1` for the batch dim in this case.

**Effect:** KServe v2 clients (`perf_analyzer`, `aiperf`, standard `tritonclient`) fail with `unable to set shape for the input` on any Dynamo-registered model with `max_batch_size > 0`. Datatype is now correct ([post-ai-dynamo/dynamo#14957](<https://github.com/post-ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/14957>) / ai-dynamo/dynamo#14520) but shape rejection blocks all requests.

**Confirmed Dynamo-specific:** identical model + image + client, Triton standalone succeeds, Dynamo fails.

## Reproduction

1. Deploy any Dynamo-registered Triton model with `max_batch_size > 0` and one or more dynamic `dims`. e.g. CLIP-L14:

   ```
   max_batch_size: 4
   input [{ name: "query", data_type: TYPE_STRING, dims: [-1] }]
   output [{ name: "text_embeddings", data_type: TYPE_FP32, dims: [-1] }]
   ```
2. Send any KServe v2 gRPC request with a batched input (e.g. `perf_analyzer -b 4 --shape query:4`).
3. Observe:

   ```
   Thread [0] had error: unable to set shape for the input
   Thread [1] had error: unable to set shape for the input
   Failed to maintain requested inference load.
   ```
4. Same request against native `tritonserver` (same model config, same image) succeeds.

## Root cause

`lib/llm/src/grpc/service/kserve.rs` at \~L688 and \~L707 (adjacent to the ai-dynamo/dynamo#14957 datatype fix):

```rust
shape: input.dims.clone(),
```

No handling of `model_config.max_batch_size`. Triton core's KServe adapter prepends `-1` to `shape` when `max_batch_size > 0`. Dynamo's `Config::Triton` branch does not.

## Suggested fix

```rust
// pseudocode
let shape = if model_config.max_batch_size > 0 {
    std::iter::once(-1i64).chain(input.dims.iter().copied()).collect()
} else {
    input.dims.clone()
};
```

Applied at both input mapping  and output mapping  in the `Config::Triton` branch.

## Related

* ai-dynamo/dynamo#14519 (Done Sep 14, Anthony Casagrande): documented the underlying protocol mismatch and recommended `max_batch_size: 0` as a **config-level workaround**. Fixed the BYTES/DLPack bugs in the `tritonserver` example. Did NOT fix the frontend metadata reporting.
* ai-dynamo/dynamo#14520 **/** #14520 **/** ai-dynamo/dynamo#14957 (Done Sep 16): sibling metadata bug (`TYPE_STRING` vs `BYTES` datatype) in the same file/branch.

Both prior tickets fixed adjacent lines of the same handler. This is the third field in the same `TensorMetadata` mapping (`shape`) with the same class of issue: raw pass-through of Triton model config without translating to KServe v2 wire semantics.

## Live evidence

* Dynamo smoke round (main + ai-dynamo/dynamo#14957): `mw_0916_smoke_dynamo_n1_A_c2/` — all 3 perf_analyzer repeats fail with `unable to set shape for the input`
* Triton smoke round (same image, same model, same driver)

Workaround exists (`max_batch_size: 0`, put batch in `dims`). But every user who follows standard Triton config conventions with `max_batch_size` will hit this on Dynamo — silent semantic divergence from native Triton.

Also discovered by @wenhant independently (Slack thread, Sep 15) though initially attributed to the ai-dynamo/dynamo#14520 datatype bug.

title: [BUG]: Invalid multimodal URIs return opaque 500 instead of a 4xx validation error
body:
### Describe the Bug

When a chat completion request embeds an image via a malformed `data:` URI, the Dynamo worker raises a plain `ValueError` during image decoding. This exception is not preserved as a client error, so it propagates as a generic backend exception and the client receives an opaque **500 "Failed to generate completions"**.

Malformed client input should produce a **4xx with a clear diagnostic message**. A 500 signals a server fault and causes clients to retry requests that can never succeed.


### Steps to Reproduce

**Variant A — invalid base64 payload:**

```bash
curl -s http://<frontend>:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"<model>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"data:image/png;base64,not!!!base64!!!"}},{"type":"text","text":"What is in this image?"}]}],"max_tokens":10}'
```

**Variant B — missing `;base64` marker:**

```bash
curl -s http://<frontend>:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"<model>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"data:image/png,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8BQDwAEhQGAhKmMIQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="}},{"type":"text","text":"What is in this image?"}]}],"max_tokens":10}'
```

**Variant C — non-image MIME type:**

```bash
curl -s http://<frontend>:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"<model>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"data:text/plain;base64,aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ="}},{"type":"text","text":"What is in this image?"}]}],"max_tokens":10}'
```

### Expected Behavior

All malformed `data:` URI inputs → 400 Bad Request with a clear message.


### Actual Behavior

All three variants return HTTP 500 with an opaque body:

```json
{"message":"Failed to generate completions","type":"Internal Server Error","code":500}
```


### Environment

- Dynamo: latest main (nightly image, deployed 2026-08-30)
- Backend: vLLM 0.27.1, disaggregated (1 prefill + 1 decode)
- Model: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct
- Deployment: DynamoGraphDeployment on Kubernetes
